summary: Bare light-grey carbon steel sheet with faint handling marks, as it comes from the stockholder.
_comment: Raw mild steel: bare, uncoated carbon-steel sheet or plate as it comes from the stockholder, light grey, unpolished, with faint handling scratches and a few small spots of fresh oxide (ambientCG Metal002, CC0; tagged steel, scratches, silver, bumpy). Opaque: a solid metal; the scan's metalness map is 1 except in the oxide spots. The source says steel, not mild steel; ordinary bare structural steel is mild steel, so the name keeps the wish list's word. The source states no physical size: the scan is judged 0.3 m across from its oxide spots (2-5 mm), and is quilted into an exact 1 m tile (tools/converters/base/quilt_scan.py, 2026-10-22, Phase19 D-9), every patch at the scan's own size, nothing stretched. Renamed from MildSteel_Raw_Clean_Base_s01_v01: a 0.1 m tile of this scan repeated its sparse oxide spots as a grid and cut its long scratches, so it takes the 1 m option. The scan's own _s01 maps stay for Paint_OnMetal_Chipped, which still uses them. APPROXIMATE: no metal edge tint (F82 specular_color) or complex IOR (F-LC-6). Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): scratches (overlay 1, damage), pitting (overlay 2, corrosion pits), dust as a deposit (Phase10), gated by the Grime mask. Built by the Phase11 batch.
name: MildSteel_Raw_Clean_Base_s1_v01

sources.why: re-makes the scan at its scale option: quilted at the scan's own size, never stretched (resampled to 1152 px first, a resolution change, so 1 m is a whole number of patch steps)

The scan judged 0.3 m across from the oxide spots (2-5 mm, 7-15 px of the 1024 px tile), since the source states no physical size. The scan's mean linear albedo (about 0.31, 0.32, 0.33) is left as scanned; it is darker than Physically Based 'Iron' (0.53, 0.513, 0.494), whose F82 tint and complex IOR the library does not carry either.
